name: service-studio-pitch
title: Making services legible to agents
notes: Pitch for Service Studio and the journey executor. Draft, November 2026.

slides.heading: Agents will use our services whether we design for them or not
slides.body: Services are built for a person with a browser. If we do not design a route, the one that appears will be one we cannot see.
slides.notes: The choice is between a mediated route we design and an unmediated one that arrives on its own.

slides.heading: What a person needs when an agent acts for them
bullets: Let me stop and come back
Nothing in my name I didn't agree to
slides.notes: The six user needs. Every part of the offer traces back to one of them.

slides.heading: Describe a service once. Run it anywhere.
slides.notes: The offer has two parts that are ours: Service Studio and the journey executor.

slides.heading: Service Studio: the department describes its own service
slides.body: What it asks, what counts as a valid answer, what order things happen in. One description for the web, the App and an agent.
slides.notes: Owned by the department, authoritative everywhere the service is met.

slides.heading: The executor runs it, one step at a time
slides.notes: Progression stays with the service. The agent only turns what the person says into structured values.

slides.heading: Where we are
bullets: GOV.UK Forms run end to end through the executor
Studio prototype drafts journeys from web pages
First discovery with DWP Maternity Allowance
slides.notes: Forms adaptor built by October. Studio prototype is on an unmerged branch: a graph editor, with an onboarding route that generates a schema from a service's web page.

slides.heading: Next: a service with real branching
What we need
bullets: A department to host the next pilot
A home for the executor in Flex
Service teams to test the proposal
slides.notes: The first two block. The third is how we learn whether departments will author descriptions themselves.
